title: metrics.py: reservoir sampling uses unseeded global random
description:
## Problem

`Metrics._add_latency_sample` uses `import random` / `random.randint` (process-global RNG) once `_latency_samples` hits `_MAX_LATENCY_SAMPLES` (10000).

`Simulation` documents `seed=` as making "the same random sequence" so chaos/jitter runs reproduce. `self._rng = random.Random(seed)` is never passed into Metrics. After 10k deliveries, p50/p95/p99 are a function of whatever else used `random` in-process (other sims, tests, libraries). Two sims with the same seed can disagree on percentiles; repeating one seed can disagree across process lifetime.

Below 10k samples the list is complete so tests stay deterministic. City-mesh / sustained-load runs cross the cap.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (`_add_latency_sample`)
- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/base.py (`self._rng` not wired to Metrics)

## Why this is robustness

Seeded sims are the reproducibility contract for chaos and SLA percentiles. Reservoir replacement from a global RNG silently breaks that contract exactly when the sample set is large enough to care about p99.
design: Give Metrics an optional rng (random.Random) defaulting to a dedicated Random(seed) or the simulation's _rng. Use rng.randint in the reservoir path. Do not call the module-level random. Tests that stay under 10k samples remain bit-identical; a unit test with a stubbed rng can force replacement.
acceptance_criteria: Two Metrics instances constructed with the same Random(seed), each recording >10000 distinct latencies in the same order, report identical p50/p95/p99. Using the process-global random module in another thread/test does not change those values.
close_reason: Metrics reservoir sampling uses a dedicated Random (Simulation seed copy), not random.randint. Identical seeds produce identical p50/p95/p99 after the 10k cap.
